title: The Shadow Inquisition
summary: The secret Church body that hunts supernatural evil.

claims.text: The Inquisition, also called the shadow or secret Inquisition, is a body inside the Catholic Church that seeks out and destroys supernatural evil.
The Holy Office is its public face, dealing with ordinary heresy; most of its members know nothing of the shadow Inquisition.
An inquisitor is a member of the shadow Inquisition, usually though not always from one of the five orders.
The game uses a real Inquisition with some dates moved, and is about how far faith and fanaticism push people, not about any real believers.

title: Councils of Faith and the Grand Inquisitor

claims.text: A Council of Faith rules the inquisitors of a large city or region, holding trials and settling disputes between them.
The Supreme Council of Faith sits in Rome.
The Grand Inquisitor heads the whole shadow Inquisition; so far in the Dark Medieval the only one has been Cardinal Battista Marzone.

title: The Five Orders
summary: The groups that supply the Inquisition's members.

claims.text: The Inquisition draws its members from five orders.
The monastic orders are the Knights of Acre, the Sisters of St. John and the Red Order; the lay orders are the Oculi Dei and the House of Murnau.
The Poor Knights of the Passion of the Cross of Acre are a military order of monk-knights who fight the enemy in battle.
The Sisters of St. John are nuns, often gifted with the Holy Sight, who protect the weak; they lean on Social traits, and most have high Self-Control.
The Order of St. Theodosius, the Red Order, is monks and nuns who have mastered the Holy Art of ritual.

title: Oculi Dei
summary: The Eyes of God, the Inquisition's spies.

claims.text: The Oculi Dei, the Eyes of God, are a secret society across Europe of lay brothers and sisters who gather word of the enemy.
Their curse, Anathemae, makes them grow jaded, then loathe and at last fear their own order, until they think it a conspiracy using them as pawns.
Their benefit is knowledge of hidden crimes and sins outside the Inquisition's remit, which they can use as blackmail.

title: The House of Murnau
summary: A Bavarian noble family pledged to the Inquisition.

claims.text: The House of Murnau is a Bavarian noble house promised as a whole to the Inquisition's service.
Its curse, Maledictio, brings strange curses and long streaks of bad luck, and often draws fiends to the cursed member.
Its members have learned to use parts of their uncanny heritage, called Legacies.

title: Conviction, Piety and the Virtues
summary: The traits that measure an inquisitor's faith.

claims.text: Conviction is the sum of the primary superior Virtue and the basic Virtues that govern it, for example Conscience plus Faith.
Starting Piety is Conscience plus Self-Control; starting Willpower is Courage plus Zeal.
The game assumes the Dark Ages: Vampire core rules and does not repeat them.

title: Blessings and Curses
summary: The God-given gifts of inquisitors and their price.

claims.text: Inquisitors wield powers given by God, and each order's gifts come with a curse.
True Faith is not a trait here; the Gifts of Faith in Dark Ages: Vampire are simple versions of these Blessings.
To work out a True Faith rating, treat Servants as one dot, Acolytes as two and so on up the ranks, so no rank reaches True Faith 5.
Ascetic means self-denial as a religious life; eremitic means living as a solitary religious withdrawn from the world.
A convent is a monastic community of men or women; a novice has entered one but not yet taken final vows.
Oblation is offering oneself or a child to God as a monk or nun. An indulgence remits punishment for acts such as crusade or pilgrimage.
